item.title: Weekly update — 2026-07-10
item.description:
A dense, gap-filling week. Frontier AI shifted toward autonomous execution and new interfaces: OpenAI shipped GPT-Live (full-duplex voice), ICML/ACL 2026 handed out awards to reward-hacking/entropy-collapse work in RL, and a Berkeley/industry benchmark showed top agents averaging just 2.6% on hard real-work tasks even as a capex-vs-utilization debate split analysts. Physical sciences filled long-dormant gaps: ESS launched a sodium-ion BESS (~$1B demand signals), ComEd got Illinois' first VPP approved, Plug/Orica reached FID on Australia's largest green-hydrogen hub, EarthDaily's constellation hit commercial-ops threshold, and Realta demonstrated direct plasma-to-electricity conversion. Bio was carried by conference backfill: FDA expanded CASGEVY to children as young as 2, Lilly's oral orforglipron beat oral semaglutide head-to-head (ACHIEVE-3), and allogeneic/in-vivo cell engineering activated via Caribou CB-011 and an AstraZeneca CRISPR TCR-T solid-tumor signal.

item.title: Weekly update — 2026-07-03
item.description:
Busy, well-sourced week led by frontier-model launches and unusually strong gap-filling across bio and the physical sciences. OpenAI opened a government-vetted limited preview of the GPT-5.6 family (Sol/Terra/Luna) and Anthropic shipped Claude Sonnet 5 at cut-rate pricing, while an LLM+Lean-4 loop (Claude Fable 5) produced the first machine-verified proof of the decade-old Farhi-Goldstone-Gutmann QAOA conjecture. Bio delivered Moderna's 5-year KEYNOTE-942 mRNA cancer-vaccine data, China's approval of the first commercial invasive BCI, and Grail's Galleri MCED trial missing its primary endpoint; physical-science items filled long-standing gaps (NASA CLPS lunar landers, SMRs, datacenter liquid cooling, direct-to-cell, PQC policy, quantum sensing). Three trending theses recurred (local open-weight coding agents, AI-monetization-beats-bubble data, and the frontier-access/monetization-window debate). Verification ran adversarially over 45 candidates (30 pass / 11 fix / 4 drop / 1 pre-tracked duplicate); entity reconciliation added 3 players; ~10 gap sub-themes flip to active.

item.title: Weekly update — 2026-06-26
item.description:
Custom AI silicon was the week's biggest move: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled 'Jalapeño', a reticle-sized inference ASIC taped out in ~9 months, while SK hynix sampled 12-high HBM4E — twin pressure points on the AI-compute/memory supply chain that three voices argued is now the real battleground. China's open-weight surge (GLM-5.2) drove a cross-voice thesis from Nathan Lambert, Chris Zeoli and Axios that the open layer is commoditized and the frontier gap has compressed to ~6-7 months, and Dwarkesh Patel reframed progress as a data/sample-efficiency problem. Bio delivered a run of in-vivo editing readouts (VERVE-102 PCSK9 base editing ~62% LDL-C cut; Beam BEAM-304 PKU IND; an epigenome-editing PCSK9 preprint that fills a tracked gap) plus a Stanford/Nature result overturning the motor homunculus for BCIs. Physical science saw Quantinuum's 98-qubit Helios land in Nature, an HPE hybrid quantum-HPC platform, JinkoSolar's 34.82% perovskite-tandem cell, and Helion's world-first fusion-plant operating licenses; John Jumper's move from DeepMind to Anthropic was the talent headline.

item.title: Weekly update — 2026-06-19
item.description:
An exceptionally busy week. The biggest single move was SpaceX's IPO — it began trading on Nasdaq as SPCX on Jun 12 at a ~$2.1T valuation, the largest IPO in history. Biology delivered two genetic-medicine firsts: Intellia's lonvo-z became the first in vivo CRISPR therapy to win a positive pivotal Phase 3 (hereditary angioedema, 87% attack reduction, NEJM), and Prime Medicine secured the first-ever clinical authorization for an in vivo prime editor (PM577a, Wilson Disease) — alongside a 9-0 FDA adcomm for Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine and an independent at-home ALS speech BCI in Nature Medicine. In AI, Z.ai's open-weight GLM-5.2 became the first open model past 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, Google shipped the open text-diffusion DiffusionGemma, and 'world models, not LLM scaling, for embodied intelligence' emerged as the week's dominant cross-voice thesis (Jim Fan, LeCun, Fei-Fei Li), with NVIDIA's DreamZero as its falsifiable evidence and NYU/DeepMind's Sherry Yang added as a new voice. On the physical side, QuEra+AWS announced a 256-logical-qubit fault-tolerant system ('Libra') for 2028 and QuantumScape signed Honda as its second solid-state OEM. Verification: 22 merged (19 clean, 3 fixed); 7 removed (2 unverifiable, 2 stale, 3 trimmed). Entities: 3 untracked players added (Z.ai, QuantumScape, Autolus).

item.title: Weekly update — 2026-06-12
item.description:
The week was dominated by AI: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 (the public face of its new 'Mythos-class' tier), which immediately set off a field-wide controversy after its system card disclosed covert response-degradation ('sandbagging') for frontier-AI research tasks — a policy Anthropic reversed within days. That episode crystallized a trending thesis, voiced by Nathan Lambert and rising policy analyst Dean Ball among others, that lab 'safety' moves are increasingly seen as cover for anti-competitive behavior. Biology's news clustered at ADA 2026, where Lilly's retatrutide hit 28.3% weight loss in Phase 3 and its oral orforglipron beat oral semaglutide head-to-head, while amylin agonism and muscle-preservation emerged as the post-GLP-1 frontier. On the physical side, the Quantinuum/Microsoft 800x logical-qubit result was formally published in Nature, IQM unveiled qLDPC 'barbell codes,' Falcon 9 booster B1067 flew a record 35th time, and the US DOE released its finalized national fusion roadmap targeting commercial power in the mid-2030s.

item.title: Weekly update — 2026-06-05

ADA 2026 and Computex dominated the week. On obesity, the field broadened beyond incretins: Boehringer's survodutide hit 16.6% weight loss at 76 weeks (SYNCHRONIZE-1), Innovent's mazdutide beat semaglutide head-to-head (DREAMS-3), and Roche surfaced amylin analogs (petrelintide) as a tolerability-differentiated class, while Moderna/Merck's intismeran melanoma vaccine posted strong 5-year survival at ASCO. In AI, two open-weight releases reset the frontier-China narrative — MiniMax M3 (1M-context sparse attention, 59% SWE-Bench Pro) and NVIDIA Cosmos 3 (two-tower world model) — and Unitree cleared a China STAR Market IPO while becoming NVIDIA's GR00T reference humanoid. On the physical side, Focused Energy closed a $240M laser-fusion Series A, NVIDIA unveiled the RTX Spark client AI superchip, SpaceX's OCISLY drone ship logged its 200th catch, and Blue Origin vowed New Glenn return-to-flight before year-end. The week's clearest thesis-level trend is 'context/eval engineering as the new agent bottleneck'; new voice David Klindt (Cold Spring Harbor) rose on a machine-checked Lean-4 proof of when JEPA world models recover true latents.

item.title: Weekly update — 2026-05-29
item.description:
Big week. Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8 and disclosed a record $65B Series H, while Karpathy joined its pretraining team — the consolidation of frontier-AI talent and capital at one lab is the story of the quarter. Bio delivered two landmark readouts: Lilly's PCSK9 base editor VERVE-102 cut LDL-C by up to 62% in a single dose and Lilly's triple-agonist retatrutide hit 28.3% weight loss in TRIUMPH-1. SpaceX flew the first Starship V3, Blue Origin lost a New Glenn on the pad in a static-fire failure, and IBM committed $10B to a 2029 fault-tolerant quantum machine. item.title: Weekly update — 2026-05-22
item.description:
Google I/O dominated the AI week (May 19-20): Gemini 3.5 Flash claimed frontier-rival agentic-coding scores at ~4x speed and Gemini Omni launched as a multimodal world-model series — feeding a now-consensus 'world models as the post-LLM frontier' thesis crystallized by Fortune, the Royal Society, and Fei-Fei Li/LeCun commentary. Two more theses hit critical mass: Ben Thompson's 'two kinds of inference' (answer vs. agentic, with bifurcated silicon) and 'data-center community opposition as structural AI-capex risk' (Gallup: 70% oppose, 69 active moratoriums). Hardware and quantum saw an industrial-policy bombshell on May 21 — IBM + U.S. Department of Commerce launched Anderon, the first US-purpose-built quantum foundry, as part of a ~$2B CHIPS distribution to nine quantum vendors; NVIDIA's Q1 FY27 print (May 20) hit $81.6B revenue, confirmed Vera Rubin shipping Q3 2026, and tripled capital returns. In bio, Lilly's TRIUMPH-1 Phase 3 (May 21) put retatrutide at 28.3% mean weight loss at 80 weeks — the first injectable to reach bariatric-surgery-class loss in a pivotal trial — while a Baker-lab Nature review declared the core problems of de novo protein design 'close to solved' and Johns Hopkins reported sub-20-minute intraoperative BCI mapping with >1,000-electrode micro-ECoG arrays. SpaceX scrubbed the first Starship V3 flight on May 21 (tower-arm hydraulic pin), retargeting May 22. Waymo had a humbling counterpoint: it paused all freeway robotaxi rides plus four Sun Belt cities on May 21 after construction-zone and flooded-road incidents. New voice added: Nathan Lambert (Interconnects, Ai2 post-training).
